title: Scout discovers new lawful sources without a human adding them
statement: The Scout Fabric runs continuously and finds new candidate sources on its own; it does not depend on a human adding each feed.
rationale: A platform that only looks where a person already thought to look never learns of the source that would have corrected its blind spot.

verification.check: A discovery pass with an empty operator list still produces new candidate sources from discovery targets; fails if candidates come only from a committed list.

notes: 'Lawful' is carried by the law/terms inspection requirement in §6.2 step 3.

title: Scout creates or proposes an adapter for an approved source
statement: For a source it approves, the Scout creates, or proposes for review, a feed adapter that can ingest it.
rationale: An approval that never becomes an adapter is a report nobody can act on.

verification.check: A registered source yields an ingestion descriptor/adapter plan matching its access mechanism; fails if registration produces no plan.

title: Access and terms of registered sources are re-checked continuously
statement: The Scout re-reads access method and legal terms of every registered source on each pass and stops using a source whose terms or access no longer permit it.
rationale: A source registered Monday whose publisher forbade the path Tuesday stays 'currently collected' if re-assessment only looks at new candidates.

verification.check: Re-assessing a registered source whose robots/terms turned against it quarantines it and removes it from the catalogue; fails if it stays registered.

title: Raw market events feed reflex path and tick fabric
statement: Raw market events feed both the live reflex path and the historical Tick Learning Fabric, subject to venue entitlements and retention rules.
rationale: A tick fabric fed separately from the reflex path learns from a different market than the one the cell traded.

verification.check: One decoded market event reaches both the cell's pass and the tick lake with its entitlement; fails if either sink is not reached.

title: Exchange and market-structure sources are acquirable
statement: The source universe includes exchange feeds, order books, trades, quotes, options surfaces, funding, borrow, rates and venue status.
rationale: A source class the fabric cannot acquire is a blind spot; one acquired without its licensing posture is a compliance breach.

verification.check: Each named source class has at least one admitted connector or a documented refusal; fails if a class has neither.

title: Filings, regulatory and official-statistics sources are acquirable
statement: The source universe includes filings, earnings, regulatory portals, court/docket data, procurement, patents, corporate registries, government statistics and central-bank releases.
rationale: A source class the fabric cannot acquire is a blind spot; one acquired without its licensing posture is a compliance breach.

verification.check: Each named source class has at least one admitted connector or a documented refusal; fails if a class has neither.

title: News, public web and public social sources are acquirable
statement: The source universe includes news, press releases, expert publications, public web, deep-web databases, public social signals and public discussion communities.
rationale: A source class the fabric cannot acquire is a blind spot; one acquired without its licensing posture is a compliance breach.

verification.check: Each named source class has at least one admitted connector or a documented refusal; fails if a class has neither.

title: Blockchain, mempool and protocol sources are acquirable
statement: The source universe includes blockchain state, mempools, token flows, smart-contract events and protocol governance.
rationale: A source class the fabric cannot acquire is a blind spot; one acquired without its licensing posture is a compliance breach.

verification.check: Each named source class has at least one admitted connector or a documented refusal; fails if a class has neither.

title: Geospatial, weather, shipping and physical-flow sources are acquirable
statement: The source universe includes geospatial/satellite, weather, shipping/AIS, flight, port, traffic, commodity flows, energy grids and public IoT where licensed/available.
rationale: A source class the fabric cannot acquire is a blind spot; one acquired without its licensing posture is a compliance breach.

verification.check: Each named source class has at least one admitted connector or a documented refusal; fails if a class has neither.

title: Product, SKU and marketplace sources are acquirable
statement: The source universe includes product/SKU listings, inventories, prices, shipping estimates, marketplace fees, auction data and resale markets.
rationale: A source class the fabric cannot acquire is a blind spot; one acquired without its licensing posture is a compliance breach.

verification.check: Each named source class has at least one admitted connector or a documented refusal; fails if a class has neither.

title: Private and user-authorised datasets only under explicit entitlement
statement: Private, alternative, licensed and user-authorised datasets are acquired only under an explicit entitlement recorded with the source.
rationale: Data used outside its licence is a regulatory and contractual breach that the event log would faithfully record.

verification.check: Constructing an event or registration without an entitlement is refused; fails if a default grant is substituted.

title: Acquisition runs fetch-parse-evidence-extract-delta-world model
statement: Acquisition proceeds SOURCE -> transient fetch -> parse/extract -> evidence check -> entity/event/fact/feature -> knowledge delta -> world models/memory.
rationale: A fetched document that skips the evidence check reaches the world model as a fact.

verification.check: A connector poll produces records that pass schema/event gates, become typed records and update the world model; fails if a gate can be bypassed.

title: Every acquisition records source manifest, content hash and cursor
statement: Each acquisition records a source manifest, a hash of exactly the bytes read, and the cursor/position reached.
rationale: Without the hash a backtest whose source silently revised its history cannot be flagged; without the cursor a restart re-reads or skips.

verification.check: A poll yields a digest whose hash matches the fetched bytes and a checkpoint that resumes to the same cursor; fails if the hash covers mapped records instead of bytes.

title: Raw external content is discarded after extraction
statement: External source payloads exist only long enough to parse, validate, extract and reason; raw external content is then discarded and durable storage begins at the knowledge boundary.
rationale: A hoard of vendor documents is a licensing liability and an unbounded store.

verification.check: A canary string in a fetched body appears in no journal, released record or digest after a poll; fails if any durable artefact holds the body.

title: Discovery starts from world-model gaps and forecast errors
statement: The discovery loop observes gaps in the world model, strategies and forecast errors and turns them into discovery targets.
rationale: Discovery driven by an operator list never reads the platform's own forecast errors, the cheapest evidence that a source is missing.

verification.check: A forecast-error spike on an uncovered entity yields a target naming it and the covering candidate is assessed first; fails if target order ignores the spike.

title: Discovery generates queries by geography, entity, domain and language
statement: From each target the loop generates source-discovery queries and candidate locations across geography, entity, domain and language.
rationale: A query without a language or geography cannot be sent, and guessing one searches the wrong corpus.

verification.check: queries_for yields one query per geography x domain x language and refuses a profile missing a dimension; fails if a dimension is defaulted.

title: Law and terms are inspected before a source is used
statement: Before registration each candidate's law/terms (licence, robots, jurisdiction) are inspected; unknown or forbidden legality is never collected regardless of score.
rationale: A high-scoring source with a forbidden licence that is collected anyway is a compliance breach recorded in the log.

verification.check: A candidate scoring 1.0 everywhere with a forbidden or unknown licence is Rejected; fails if Routing can be built from score alone.

notes: Also the §6 intro's 'lawful' and the rule 'licensing posture evaluated before a source is used'.

title: Candidate access, schema, freshness and cost are inspected
statement: Each candidate's access method, schema, freshness and cost are inspected from probe evidence before registration.
rationale: Registering on the candidate's own description of itself is registering on hearsay.

verification.check: A registered source's trail records a finding for each inspection attribute; fails if any attribute is unrecorded.

title: Candidate uniqueness and manipulation risk are inspected
statement: Each candidate's expected uniqueness and manipulation risk are assessed, and a source showing manipulation evidence is not registered.
rationale: A source serving records dated after they were fetched admits point-in-time leakage through the front door.

verification.check: A candidate whose records are dated after the probe is refused on manipulation risk; fails if freshness rewards the future-dated payload.

title: Approved source metadata is registered with a named operator
statement: Approved source metadata is registered in a catalogue; the registration carries the legality assessment and a named operator.
rationale: An anonymous or assessment-free registration cannot be audited.

verification.check: Registration without a legal assessment or with a blank operator is refused; fails if a catalogue entry exists without either.

title: A new source's adapter runs in a sandbox before promotion
statement: A newly registered source's feed/adapter is instantiated in a sandbox, and its output reaches knowledge stores only after a recorded promotion.
rationale: An unproven adapter writing straight into the world model contaminates every belief it touches.

verification.check: A sandboxed source's records do not reach the world model until a promotion event; fails if sandbox output is ingested.

title: Source scored on incremental information gain
statement: A source is scored on incremental information gain over the sources already held.
rationale: A source kept on reputation rather than measured value is a cost with no edge.

verification.check: The named score changes in the expected direction for a duplicate vs informative (or late vs early, flaky vs stable) source; fails if the score ignores its input.

title: Source scored on timeliness
statement: A source is scored on timeliness, measured as how far its facts lead the same fact elsewhere.
rationale: A source kept on reputation rather than measured value is a cost with no edge.

verification.check: The named score changes in the expected direction for a duplicate vs informative (or late vs early, flaky vs stable) source; fails if the score ignores its input.

title: Source scored on reliability
statement: A source is scored on reliability from observed availability, errors and latency.
rationale: A source kept on reputation rather than measured value is a cost with no edge.

verification.check: The named score changes in the expected direction for a duplicate vs informative (or late vs early, flaky vs stable) source; fails if the score ignores its input.

title: Source scored on realised strategy contribution
statement: A source is scored on its realised contribution to strategy outcomes once used.
rationale: A source kept on reputation rather than measured value is a cost with no edge.

verification.check: The named score changes in the expected direction for a duplicate vs informative (or late vs early, flaky vs stable) source; fails if the score ignores its input.

title: Sources promoted automatically under policy
statement: Policy automatically promotes a registered source on re-assessment evidence, with no operator step, and journals the transition.
rationale: A lifecycle that needs a person to act is a lifecycle that does not happen at 3 a.m.

verification.check: A re-assessment pass whose evidence warrants it yields a promote transition journaled in the event log; fails if the registry is unchanged.

notes: §6.2 step 6 split per action; §6 intro 'retires low-value sources' folded into the retire row.

title: Sources throttled automatically under policy
statement: Policy automatically throttles a registered source on re-assessment evidence, with no operator step, and journals the transition.
rationale: A lifecycle that needs a person to act is a lifecycle that does not happen at 3 a.m.

verification.check: A re-assessment pass whose evidence warrants it yields a throttle transition journaled in the event log; fails if the registry is unchanged.

notes: §6.2 step 6 split per action; §6 intro 'retires low-value sources' folded into the retire row.

title: Sources quarantined automatically under policy
statement: Policy automatically quarantines a registered source on re-assessment evidence, with no operator step, and journals the transition.
rationale: A lifecycle that needs a person to act is a lifecycle that does not happen at 3 a.m.

verification.check: A re-assessment pass whose evidence warrants it yields a quarantine transition journaled in the event log; fails if the registry is unchanged.

notes: §6.2 step 6 split per action; §6 intro 'retires low-value sources' folded into the retire row.

title: Sources retired automatically under policy
statement: Policy automatically retires a registered source on re-assessment evidence, with no operator step, and journals the transition.
rationale: A lifecycle that needs a person to act is a lifecycle that does not happen at 3 a.m.

verification.check: A re-assessment pass whose evidence warrants it yields a retire transition journaled in the event log; fails if the registry is unchanged.

notes: §6.2 step 6 split per action; §6 intro 'retires low-value sources' folded into the retire row.

title: No single source is truth; beliefs update from evidence
statement: Extracted claims update beliefs through evidence weighting; no single source and no scraped text is converted directly into a fact.
rationale: Scraped text promoted straight to fact makes one wrong article a world-model truth.

verification.check: No finite evidence drives a belief to certainty and contradicting evidence lowers it; fails if a single item sets the belief to 1.

title: Every extracted claim becomes an Evidence object with full provenance
statement: Every extracted claim becomes an Evidence object carrying source identity, timestamp, location, extraction method, authenticity signals, license and confidence.
rationale: A claim without provenance cannot be re-checked or retracted.

verification.check: Constructing evidence without source, extraction method or license is refused, and every ingested world claim is wrapped; fails if a claim reaches the world model without one.

title: Evidence links to corroborating and contradicting evidence
statement: Each Evidence object carries links to the evidence that corroborates or contradicts it.
rationale: Without links a contradiction cannot be traced back to the claims it involves.

verification.check: Linking two evidence items records the relation on both sides and survives replay; fails if links are dropped.

title: A provenance graph of evidence is built
statement: The system builds a provenance graph linking claims to sources and to each other.
rationale: A belief whose evidence chain cannot be walked cannot be audited.

verification.check: From a belief, walking the graph reaches every source document hash it rests on; fails if any edge is missing.

title: Authenticity signals are recorded and checked
statement: Authenticity is assessed from TLS/domain identity, signed releases where available, document hashes, chain proofs, known issuer identity and source history.
rationale: A spoofed release from a look-alike domain is otherwise indistinguishable from the real one.

verification.check: Evidence from a verified-hash, registered-issuer source outranks an unsigned copy; fails if authenticity has no effect on weight.

title: Corroboration discounts common-source dependence
statement: Corroboration is weighted by independent-source agreement so that copies of one origin (ten copies of one press release) count as one source.
rationale: Ten syndicated copies counted as ten confirmations manufacture certainty from one claim.

verification.check: Adding copies of an existing origin leaves supporting weight unchanged while a new origin raises it; fails if a per-copy increment is reintroduced.

title: Claims are checked for temporal consistency
statement: Each claim is checked against prior state, event ordering and physically possible timelines, and the result is recorded.
rationale: A claim ingested before its source published it, or an effect dated before its cause, is a fabrication or a leak.

verification.check: A claim dated after its publication or before its declared cause is marked inconsistent; fails if marked Consistent.

title: Claims are checked for geospatial consistency
statement: Location, routing, shipping, weather and jurisdiction evidence must agree where relevant, and disagreement is recorded.
rationale: A shipment reported in two ports at once is a data error that would otherwise drive a trade.

verification.check: Two claims placing one entity in incompatible locations are marked inconsistent; fails if no check runs.

title: Contradictions kept as competing hypotheses until resolved
statement: Conflicting evidence is not deleted; competing hypotheses are maintained and the later evidence that resolves them is tracked.
rationale: Deleting the losing side of a conflict makes the belief unauditable and unrevisable.

verification.check: A contradiction is recorded with both sides retained and later resolved with the resolving evidence named; fails if either side is removed.

title: Adversarial and poisoned sources are detected
statement: The fabric detects spam, coordinated manipulation, synthetic content, poisoned feeds, spoofing and anomalous source behaviour.
rationale: A coordinated campaign across outlets is invisible to any per-item check.

verification.check: A planted coordinated campaign (same timing, near-identical text across origins) is flagged; fails if the detector returns no finding.

title: Quantum methods never confer authenticity or truth
statement: Quantum optimisation/clustering on evidence graphs is optional and experimental, and no quantum output may set authenticity or truth.
rationale: 'We used a quantum computer' is not evidence of anything.

verification.check: No path from a quantum result type to an authenticity or belief field; fails if one compiles.

title: Raw tick storage is separated from the cognitive context
statement: Raw market-event storage is separate from the cognitive layer, which consumes time-aligned states, embeddings, regimes, reaction summaries and exception episodes rather than raw ticks.
rationale: Feeding billions of raw ticks to a generalist model is cost without information.

verification.check: Replay/training crates are absent from the reflex binary and the cognitive layer has no raw-tick input type; fails if it gains one.

title: Every raw tick is retained for exact replay where licensed
statement: Every raw tick remains available for exact replay and retraining, subject to entitlement.
rationale: A tick not retained is a backtest that can never be reproduced.

verification.check: A captured session can be re-materialised byte-for-byte from the lake; fails if any captured tick is missing.

title: Trades, quotes, top-of-book and L1-L3 depth are captured
statement: The tick universe includes trades, bid/ask quotes, NBBO or venue top-of-book, L1/L2 depth and L3 order-level data where licensed and economically justified.
rationale: A market fact the fabric never captured is a reaction the platform cannot learn.

verification.check: Each named event type has a typed record and a capture path; fails if a type is absent.

title: Auctions, halts, status, rejects, cancels and acks are captured
statement: The tick universe includes auction/open/close/imbalance events, halts, circuit breakers, venue status, rejects, cancels and order acknowledgements.
rationale: A market fact the fabric never captured is a reaction the platform cannot learn.

verification.check: Each named event type has a typed record and a capture path; fails if a type is absent.

title: Options, vol surfaces, futures curves, borrow and funding are captured
statement: The tick universe includes options chains, implied-volatility surfaces, Greeks, futures curves, basis, borrow, funding and financing state.
rationale: A market fact the fabric never captured is a reaction the platform cannot learn.

verification.check: Each named event type has a typed record and a capture path; fails if a type is absent.

title: FX, rates, crypto books, perp funding and on-chain state are captured
statement: The tick universe includes FX and rates quotes, crypto order books, perpetual funding, liquidations, mempool/on-chain signals and decentralised venue state.
rationale: A market fact the fabric never captured is a reaction the platform cannot learn.

verification.check: Each named event type has a typed record and a capture path; fails if a type is absent.

title: Internal order telemetry is captured as tick data
statement: The tick universe includes the platform's own submitted orders, timestamps, routing decisions, fills, partial fills, slippage, queue estimates, cancels, rejects, hedges and risk vetoes.
rationale: The platform's own executions are the only ground truth for fill and slippage models; not capturing them means calibrating to fiction.

verification.check: Every order lifecycle event, slippage and veto appears in the captured record with a trace id; fails if one is dropped.

title: Cross-asset and cross-region synchronisation metadata is kept
statement: Captured events carry cross-asset and cross-region synchronisation metadata so reactions can be learned across instruments and venues.
rationale: A market fact the fabric never captured is a reaction the platform cannot learn.

verification.check: Each named event type has a typed record and a capture path; fails if a type is absent.

title: Capture keeps source sequence, exchange time and receive time
statement: Venue capture adapters decode native feeds preserving source sequence numbers, exchange timestamps and receive timestamps.
rationale: Without the venue sequence a gap is invisible; without both clocks a backlog is invisible.

verification.check: A decoded event exposes venue sequence, exchange time and receive time as distinct values; fails if any is collapsed.

title: Raw venue messages preserved where rights allow
statement: Capture preserves raw venue messages where rights allow, and keeps the payload hash where they do not.
rationale: Without raw bytes a decoder bug can never be re-run against the original.

verification.check: A permitting entitlement stores raw bytes and a non-permitting one stores only the hash; fails if bytes are stored without rights.

title: Event, receive and normalized time and uncertainty stay distinct
statement: Normalisation preserves event time, receive time, sequence, venue and clock uncertainty as distinct fields rather than collapsing them to one timestamp.
rationale: A collapsed timestamp hides queueing and makes leakage undetectable.

verification.check: Round-tripping a canonical event preserves all three times and the uncertainty; fails if any is overwritten.

notes: §8.5 'No timestamp laundering' restates this and adds lineage of clock corrections; that half is its own requirement.

title: PTP/GPS-grade clock discipline where justified
statement: Capture nodes use PTP/GPS-grade clock discipline where the strategy justifies it, and publish the resulting uncertainty.
rationale: An unknown clock offset is a fake lead/lag signal.

verification.check: A disciplined node's published uncertainty bounds its measured offset against a reference; fails if offset exceeds the bound.

title: Canonical typed market-event schema for all event kinds
statement: Trades, quotes, depth updates, auctions, status and lifecycle events normalise into typed canonical records.
rationale: Untyped records let a field change meaning silently.

verification.check: Each event kind decodes to its typed variant; fails if any kind lands in a generic bucket.

title: Canonical records retain source payload hash and lineage
statement: Every canonical record retains the source-native payload hash and lineage.
rationale: A canonical record whose source bytes cannot be identified cannot be re-derived after a decoder fix.

verification.check: Constructing a MarketEvent with a hash for a different payload is refused; fails if the hash is trusted.

title: Immutable, checksummed, partitioned Tick Lake with manifests
statement: The Tick Lake stores partitioned historical raw/canonical events immutably, with checksums and reproducible manifests.
rationale: A rewritable history is a backtest that can be made to say anything.

verification.check: A sealed segment cannot be overwritten and a manifest re-materialises to matching checksums; fails on any accepted overwrite or unflagged corrupt byte.

title: Tick Lake partitions enforce entitlement and retention
statement: Lake partitions carry their entitlement and retention class, and a job reads only partitions it is entitled to.
rationale: A training job that can read every partition trains on data it may not use.

verification.check: A job granted one entitlement materialises only that partition; market-class objects have a delete lifecycle and internal-class never deletes; fails otherwise.

title: Tick Lake compresses segments
statement: Lake segments are compressed.
rationale: Uncompressed tick history multiplies storage cost.

verification.check: A written segment is smaller than its input and round-trips exactly; fails if stored uncompressed.

notes: A codec conflicts with ADR 0002/0009 (two dependencies) unless written in-tree.

title: Hot replay indexes separated from cold archive
statement: Hot replay indexes are kept separate from the cold archive so replay can seek without scanning archives.
rationale: A replay that scans the archive for every seek is too slow to use.

verification.check: Reading record N uses the manifest's index and fetches only its byte range; fails if the whole object is read.

title: Order books rebuild deterministically with checkpoints
statement: Venue books are rebuilt deterministically from canonical events, with snapshots/checkpoints.
rationale: A non-deterministic rebuild makes every replay a different market.

verification.check: Replaying one session twice and from a checkpoint yields identical books, fills and flags; fails on any divergence.

title: Reconstruction detects gaps and out-of-order events
statement: Book reconstruction detects sequence gaps and out-of-order events.
rationale: A book built over a missing increment is wrong from then on and nothing says so.

verification.check: Removing one message or reordering one beyond the window is detected; fails if the book is published.

title: Unreliable reconstruction periods are marked on output
statement: Periods where reconstruction is unreliable are marked on the replay output.
rationale: A training job that reads a flagged span as ground truth learns from a fabricated book.

verification.check: A gap yields an UnreliablePeriod on the output until the next Reset; fails if the span is unflagged.

title: Cross-venue alignment preserves uncertainty without artificial simultaneity
statement: Asynchronous instruments are aligned by event time and information arrival, preserving uncertainty and never asserting an order the clocks cannot support.
rationale: Sorting two venues on a timestamp column manufactures lead/lag that does not exist.

verification.check: Events within combined uncertainty are reported unordered; fails if the aligner orders them.

title: Microstructure feature engine computes the named feature families
statement: The feature engine generates spread, depth, imbalance, queue, flow, toxicity, volatility, liquidity, lead/lag and cross-venue features.
rationale: A model starved of microstructure features cannot learn execution.

verification.check: Each named family has a feature with a hand-computed test; fails if any family is absent.

title: Learned embedding representations of market state
statement: The representation engine produces learned embeddings of market state.
rationale: Hand-crafted features cap what the cognitive layer can see.

verification.check: An embedding model is trained, versioned and evaluated against a baseline; fails if no artefact.

title: Outcome labels built for fill, return, selection, impact, vol and decay
statement: The label builder creates fill-probability, future-return, adverse-selection, market-impact, realised-volatility, opportunity-decay and multi-horizon outcome labels.
rationale: Without labels no execution model can be trained or scored.

verification.check: Each label matches a hand computation; fails on a sign or window error.

title: Labels are built without future leakage
statement: Labels are never available as inputs at or before the instant they describe, and a window the series does not cover is refused rather than shortened.
rationale: A label that leaks into its own features produces a model that is perfect in backtest and useless live.

verification.check: A horizon past the series end is refused; a dataset whose feature timestamp exceeds its label anchor is refused; fails if accepted.

title: Replay engine replays history and decisions with execution realism
statement: The replay/simulation engine replays canonical historical markets and the platform's decisions with latency, queue, fees, rejects, partial fills, impact and multi-leg execution semantics.
rationale: A replay that ignores latency, queue and impact credits strategies with fills that never existed.

verification.check: A decision replayed against history incurs latency, fees, partial fill and impact; fails if any is zeroed.

title: Microstructure models are trained and calibrated
statement: A training service trains/calibrates specialist, execution, liquidity, slippage, fill, regime and short-horizon models.
rationale: Execution models never trained on microstructure are guesses.

verification.check: A fill-probability model trained on labelled ticks beats its baseline on holdout; fails if no such model is produced.

title: Microstructure models benchmarked by venue, asset, regime and horizon
statement: Microstructure models are benchmarked separately by venue, asset, regime and horizon.
rationale: An average across venues hides the venue where the model is wrong.

verification.check: An evaluation report has one row per venue x asset x regime x horizon; fails if aggregated.

title: Slow intelligence distilled into bounded reflex artefacts
statement: Slow/warm intelligence is distilled into bounded features, models or lookup structures that reflex nodes evaluate within their latency budgets.
rationale: A model the hot path cannot bound in time is a model that blows the latency budget under load.

verification.check: A distilled student has a stated worst-case cost and fidelity to its teacher and loads in the edge cell; fails if unbounded or unfaithful.

title: Online drift measures residuals, fill error and venue change
statement: Live residuals, fill/slippage error, regime drift and venue changes are measured continuously.
rationale: A model drifting silently trades on yesterday's market.

verification.check: A shifted feature distribution raises the drift score and the model card becomes ineligible; fails if the score stays zero.

title: Drift feeds retraining, never silent adaptation of money-moving logic
statement: Drift and feedback feed retraining and curriculum tasks; money-moving logic is never silently adapted.
rationale: A model that rewrites its own structure at millisecond cadence is a model no human reviewed trading capital.

verification.check: An update outside its cadence's permitted scope is refused; fails if a fast update changes model structure.

title: Strategies evaluated against the market that existed
statement: A strategy is evaluated against the recorded market that existed, never against bars constructed after the fact.
rationale: Bars built afterwards embed information no trader had at the time.

sources.section: §8.3 Market Replay, Counterfactual Execution and Synthetic Experience

verification.check: A decision view cannot read a bar before its close time; fails if a same-day bar is visible intraday.

title: Replay models data arrival and decision latency
statement: The simulator models what the platform could have known at each instant, including data arrival delays and decision latency.
rationale: Assuming instant arrival and decision credits strategies with a speed nobody has.

sources.section: §8.3 Market Replay, Counterfactual Execution and Synthetic Experience

verification.check: Delayed-feed and latency conditions push the execution later and worsen fills; fails if they have no effect.

title: Replay models venue rate limits
statement: The simulator enforces venue rate limits on replayed order flow.
rationale: A replay that ignores rate limits fills orders the venue would have rejected.

sources.section: §8.3 Market Replay, Counterfactual Execution and Synthetic Experience

verification.check: Orders beyond the venue's message budget are refused in replay; fails if they fill.

title: Exact historical replay with checkpoints and integrity flags
statement: Exact historical replay sequences events deterministically from venue-native/canonical records with book checkpoints and integrity flags.
rationale: A replay that is not exact cannot be used to reproduce a decision.

sources.section: §8.3 Market Replay, Counterfactual Execution and Synthetic Experience

verification.check: Same session replayed twice and from a checkpoint gives identical event order, books, fills and flags; fails on any difference.

notes: Overlaps §8.2 'Order-book reconstruction'; kept because §8.3 states it as the replay product.

title: Counterfactual replay of taken, vetoed and missed actions
statement: Actions taken, vetoed or missed are compared against feasible alternatives using only the information set available at that time.
rationale: A system that only records its trades cannot tell a calibrated gate from a shut one.

sources.section: §8.3 Market Replay, Counterfactual Execution and Synthetic Experience

verification.check: A refused order is priced once its horizon passes against a view fixed at decision time; fails if the alternative reads later data.

title: Multi-leg arbitrage replay of 2-20 legs
statement: Replay models 2-20-leg opportunity discovery, reservation, legging risk, path decay, partial execution, hedge/unwind and capital consumption across regions.
rationale: A multi-leg opportunity that disappears mid-execution leaves an unhedged leg; a replay that assumes atomic completion hides that.

sources.section: §8.3 Market Replay, Counterfactual Execution and Synthetic Experience

verification.check: A replayed 3-leg cycle whose second venue fails mid-execution yields a hedge/unwind with its cost; fails if completion is assumed.

title: Agent/market simulation generates rare regimes and stress
statement: Agent/market simulation generates synthetic rare regimes, liquidity droughts, manipulation patterns, venue outages and stress events.
rationale: Real history has too few crises to learn from.

sources.section: §8.3 Market Replay, Counterfactual Execution and Synthetic Experience

verification.check: Each named stress class can be generated deterministically from a seed; fails if a class is unavailable.

title: Execution digital twin continuously calibrated to live telemetry
statement: Fill, queue, impact and latency models of the execution twin are continuously calibrated to the platform's own telemetry.
rationale: Paper and replay assumptions that never meet reality drift into fiction.

sources.section: §8.3 Market Replay, Counterfactual Execution and Synthetic Experience

verification.check: After fills with systematic error the twin's model parameters move toward the observed fills; fails if parameters are static.

notes: 'Live telemetry' here can only be paper/simulated fills under ADR 0003.

title: Time-aligned fusion layer joins world and market intelligence
statement: A time-aligned fusion layer combines world intelligence (events, entities, beliefs, propagation paths) with market intelligence (reaction, regime, liquidity, flow, dislocation, feasibility).
rationale: Knowing an event happened without knowing whether a tradable reaction still exists is not actionable.

title: No look-ahead: only data observable by the decision instant
statement: Training and replay use only data observable by the decision timestamp, including realistic publication and feed-arrival delays.
rationale: Look-ahead produces a backtest that measures the leak.

verification.check: Any read at decision time t returns only records with known_at <= t (with delay); fails if a later record is visible.

title: No impossible fills in replay
statement: A replayed trade respects available depth, queue/priority, rate limits, latency, partial fills, venue rules and price impact.
rationale: A fill larger than the book is profit that never existed.

verification.check: No replayed fill exceeds resting depth; an alternative beyond calibrated participation is unfillable; fails if either fills.

title: Clock corrections are lineage-tracked
statement: Source, receive and normalized time and their uncertainty remain distinct, and every clock correction is recorded in lineage.
rationale: An undocumented clock correction is a laundered timestamp.

verification.check: A corrected timestamp carries a ClockCorrection record that survives into the stored event; fails if the correction is lost.

title: No hidden survivorship in historical universes
statement: Delisted instruments, venue outages, symbol changes, corporate actions and failed products remain represented in historical universes.
rationale: A backtest over survivors only overstates every strategy.

verification.check: members_as_of a past date includes an instrument delisted later; a replay across an outage reports it; fails otherwise.

title: Model artefacts record training-data entitlements and permitted use
statement: Model artefacts record which licensed market data trained them and where the artefact and its outputs are permitted to run or be used.
rationale: A model trained on data licensed for one region and run in another breaches the licence invisibly.

verification.check: A model card carries its training entitlements and permitted locations, and deployment to a non-permitted location is refused; fails if accepted.

title: Tick models must prove value over simpler baselines
statement: Models and the Evaluation Brain must prove incremental predictive or execution value versus simpler baselines; raw tick volume is not credited by itself.
rationale: Complexity that cannot beat a baseline is cost and overfitting.

verification.check: A model whose holdout skill does not beat the baseline is refused registration as skilled; fails if registered.
